questions.competencyTargeted: Background & Career Orientation
questions.promptStem: Welcome! To start off, could you give me a brief overview of your engineering background, your primary technical stack, and the kind of technical challenges you've been focused on recently?
expectedConcepts: Engineering trajectory and education/experience
Primary language and architectural focus
Interest in technical challenges
counterFactualProbes: What motivated your focus on this specific technical stack?
What type of engineering problems do you enjoy tackling most?

strongCriteria: Articulates a crisp engineering trajectory and core strengths
Mentions concrete technologies and systems built
Communicates with structured clarity
adequateCriteria: Gives a general overview of background and past coursework/jobs
Mentions basic programming skills
shallowCriteria: Extremely brief (under 10 words) or vague without mentioning any technical domain
Evades question entirely

questions.competencyTargeted: System Architecture: Full-Stack Web Application
questions.promptStem: In your Full-Stack Web Application project, you used Node.js, React, PostgreSQL. Can you walk me through the exact end-to-end data flow of a critical request through your system architecture, from client ingress to database persistence?
expectedConcepts: Request ingress & routing
Business logic execution
Database transaction boundaries & state management
Caching, connection pooling, or asynchronous decoupling
counterFactualProbes: What happens if incoming request traffic spikes 10x in a 60-second window?
How does your architecture handle network partitions between services?

strongCriteria: Traces exact request lifecycles with protocol details (HTTP/gRPC/Kafka)
Explains database transaction boundaries, locking, and caching layers
Identifies potential bottlenecks and single points of failure
adequateCriteria: Describes high-level client-server flow
Mentions database read/write without deep latency considerations
shallowCriteria: Only recites buzzwords without explaining actual data flow
Unable to describe how data reaches storage or where validation occurs

questions.competencyTargeted: Technical Ownership & Trade-offs: Full-Stack Web Application
questions.promptStem: Regarding Full-Stack Web Application, You noted: "Full stack engineering and database design". What was your specific personal contribution to the code, and what was the most significant technical trade-off you evaluated when choosing Node.js over alternatives?
expectedConcepts: Individual code ownership vs libraries/templates
Trade-off analysis (latency, consistency, complexity, developer velocity)
Alternative technologies evaluated and why they were rejected
counterFactualProbes: If you rebuilt Full-Stack Web Application from scratch today, what architectural decision would you change?
Why didn't you choose a managed cloud service or simpler framework for this component?

strongCriteria: Crisply distinguishes personal implementation from external frameworks and boilerplate
Provides quantitative or architectural trade-off justification
Acknowledges system limitations candidly and thoughtfully
adequateCriteria: Identifies features worked on personally
Offers generic justification for technology choice (e.g., 'it was popular' or 'team familiarity')
shallowCriteria: Vague regarding individual code ownership vs boilerplate
Cannot explain why alternative technologies were rejected

questions.competencyTargeted: Failure Modes & Concurrency: Full-Stack Web Application
questions.promptStem: In Full-Stack Web Application, You highlighted tackling: "Concurrency under simultaneous writes; Latency optimization". Walk me through a challenging production outage, concurrency race condition, or data inconsistency you encountered, and how did you diagnose and resolve it?
expectedConcepts: Systematic debugging and root-cause analysis
Concurrency, locking, race conditions, or network retries
Idempotency, schema constraints, or circuit-breaker remediation
counterFactualProbes: How do you prevent duplicate side-effects if a client retries this operation after an intermittent network timeout?
What observability metrics or alerts would have warned you before users noticed?

strongCriteria: Explains root-cause mechanism with concrete technical precision
Describes preventative architecture (idempotency keys, optimistic locking, bounded retry loops)
Details observability tooling and diagnostic workflows used
adequateCriteria: Describes a standard bug fix without deep systemic analysis
Mentions basic logging or restarting the service
shallowCriteria: Claims no bugs or production issues ever occurred
Unable to describe a technical debugging process

questions.competencyTargeted: Practical Problem Solving & Data Structures
questions.promptStem: Let's work through a practical systems problem: suppose we need to build an in-memory rate limiter that restricts each user to 100 API requests per minute. What data structure would you select, and how do you handle memory cleanup and high concurrency?
expectedConcepts: Sliding window counter or token bucket algorithm
Hash map with thread-safe / atomic access
TTL or periodic background cleanup of expired buckets
Time complexity O(1) per check
counterFactualProbes: Why choose a sliding window log over a fixed token bucket?
What if multiple application servers handle requests for the same user concurrently?

strongCriteria: Proposes token bucket or sliding window counter with accurate time/space bounds
Identifies concurrency race conditions on counter increments
Addresses memory leak mitigation for inactive users
adequateCriteria: Proposes fixed-window counter with basic hash map
Recognizes that stale keys need expiration
shallowCriteria: Proposes unbounded array or linear scan
Fails to consider memory growth or concurrent requests

questions.competencyTargeted: API Design & Data Validation
questions.promptStem: Suppose you are designing a RESTful API for an order checkout system. What HTTP status codes, request idempotency headers, and error handling structures would you put in place to ensure that a client retry doesn't create duplicate orders?
expectedConcepts: Idempotency-Key header standard
Unique constraints in database schema
HTTP status codes (201 Created, 200 OK, 409 Conflict, 422 Unprocessable)
Atomic transaction spanning order creation and payment authorization
counterFactualProbes: What happens if two concurrent requests arrive with the exact same idempotency key at the exact same millisecond?
How long should idempotency keys be retained in the storage layer?

strongCriteria: Designs end-to-end idempotency mechanism using unique keys and atomic transactions
Uses accurate HTTP status codes and structured RFC 7807 error responses
Separates validation errors from infrastructure failures
adequateCriteria: Mentions checking if order exists before inserting
Uses standard 200 and 400 status codes
shallowCriteria: Does not understand idempotency or suggests returning 200 for all responses
Cannot explain how duplicate orders are prevented

questions.competencyTargeted: Engineering Collaboration & Candidate Inquiries
questions.promptStem: We have covered great technical ground today across your projects, architecture, and systems engineering. To wrap up, what questions do you have for me about our engineering challenges, stack, or team culture?
expectedConcepts: Curiosity about technical architecture and stack
Questions regarding engineering practices, testing, and team growth
Professional engineering engagement
counterFactualProbes: Is there any particular architectural area or project you'd like to highlight before we conclude?

strongCriteria: Asks insightful questions about technical trade-offs, architecture, or roadmap
Shows genuine passion for engineering craft and team collaboration
adequateCriteria: Asks standard questions about team size or daily routine
shallowCriteria: No questions or completely disengaged
